thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: realtime-p99-detector firing for /v1/generate (us-west-2). p99 = 3.6s, baseline p99 = 0.45s. paging oncall@rotation. severity: P1 :rotating_light:

alex: oncall here, acknowledging. i'll start triage. which namespace? is this all regions or just us-west-2?

maria: looks concentrated in us-west-2 per the dashboard. windows of elevated p95/p99 starting ~1744442100 (about 2m ago). p95 ~ 1.1s, p99 ~ 3.6s. streaming stall rate up too (streaming stalls per 1k requests +7x). grafana: https://grafana.redwood/real-time/latency?region=us-west-2

sam: checking infra now — k8s node pressure spike around that time, a few worker pods restarted in runtime pool. `kubectl get pods -n runtime -o wide | grep CrashLoop` shows 3 restarts across instance-group-rt-3.

jeni: have we rolled anything in the last 30m? model rollout or config change?

eng-runtime: i see a canary rollout for model: text-gen-2q started ~1744441600 but should be limited to 2% traffic. routing logs show some requests routed to the new variant and to a quantized fallback. kv-cache miss rate spiked from 5% -> 48% at the same time.

alex: kv-cache miss spike sounds relevant. if kv cache misses, latency goes to full model inference and SLOs suffer. can someone run quick query on redis/kvcache metrics?

sam: running quick k/v metrics: `redis-cli --latency` shows avg command latency ~15ms (normal). but application-level key miss trace indicates a purge/reconnect event around 1744442050, many cache misses thereafter. possible connection churn.

maria: i pulled traces — tail traces show many requests hitting cold kv and then long model init path. stacktrace points to session rehydration + large prompt lengths for a subset of requests. median seq_len for p99 traces ~1200 tokens (vs baseline 150).

cs-bot: Customer Impact: 12 customers with heavy usage in us-west-2 report degraded responses (timeouts or >2s responses). No full outage. severity communicated to CS: "degraded performance". ticket created: CS-5921.

alex: immediate mitigation options: 1) roll back canary 2) force routing to cached variant 3) bump replicas for runtime pool 4) enable temporary rate-limit for long-seq requests. Which one is least risky / fastest?

jeni: safest quick action is to force route to stable model variant and enable fallback to the small-model static-cache for streaming clients. rollback canary if we detect it's in-path beyond 2% (routing policy bug?).

eng-runtime: i can flip the routing policy to prefer stable model in ~1m. command:```
# switch routing policy to preferred stable
redwoodctl routing set-policy --region us-west-2 --endpoint /v1/generate --policy prefer:stable
```

sam: i'll scale runtime pool by +30% and watch node pressure. `k scale deploy runtime-pool --replicas=13 -n runtime`

maria: surface-level checks post-actions: watch p99 panel, streaming stall rate, kv miss rate. also check autoscaler events — we might have low headroom causing queueing.

(incident-bot adds: note: autoscaler triggered 2x scale events at 1744442005 but nodes didn't come up due to capacity error on instance-group-rt-3)

alex: okay eng-runtime, flip routing. sam scale now. jen, notify cs and ask them to send proactive note to affected customers with estimated mitigation ETA 15m.

eng-runtime: routing policy change applied. logs show >90% traffic now hitting stable model.

sam: scale command accepted. pods are scheduling; one zone reported insufficient capacity so we have a small imbalance but overall replicas increasing.

maria: 30s after mitigation: p95 down to 0.9s, p99 down to 1.4s, streaming stalls dropping. kv-cache miss still elevated (28%) but improving.

cs-bot: CS update: initial customer note sent. several customers acknowledged and asked for ETA.

alex: good. next: 1) root cause analysis path — confirm whether canary routing bug or k/v purge caused miss surge. 2) open incident timeline doc and link to follow-up RCA. 3) keep paging if p99 rises again. who will own the RCA?

jeni: i'll drive RCA with eng-runtime + ops-sre. immediate hypothesis: canary rollout created a hotter cold-start pattern and a kv reconnect from infra changes caused misses to amplify. we'll collect: routing logs, kv connection logs, autoscaler events, machine capacity errors.

eng-runtime: capturing logs and saving traces to s3: s3://incidents/1744442222/traces.tar.gz. adding queries for route headers to confirm fraction of traffic.

sam: i'll follow up on instance-group capacity error with cloud infra and propose a temporary quota bump for the group if needed.

alex: handoff plan: i'll stay on until metrics stabilize for 15m and then hand to morning oncall @maria in the 30m window. if p99 > 2s again, page immediately.

maria: ack. i'll prepare a short post-incident summary template with customers impacted and timeline.

(incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated -> watching. participants: alex, maria, sam, jeni, eng-runtime, ops-sre, cs-bot)

alex: closing note: no data exfiltrated, no errors seen in auth logs, just degraded latency. will convert this into a follow-up RCA ticket and include mitigation steps for future auto-fallback and more conservative canary throttles. :white_check_mark:
